prerequisites: Recommended to have drawing knowledge, at the level of high school studies.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with basic knowledge of computer-aided design techniques.
Develop the ability to see or imagine geometric shapes in space and mentally perform operations with them.
Enable students to understand tasks, synthesize ideas, and identify with technical language as a means of communication.
Acquire proficiency in handling drawing instruments and sketching parts as a means to quickly and accurately express graphic ideas.
For students to know and value standardization as a universal means of graphic language.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing geometric constructions.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing representation systems for interpreting and representing engineering drawings.
Be able to know and apply representation standards and incorporate the use of technical terms in language.
Be able to know, understand, and use computer-aided design programs to represent engineering drawings.
Be able to understand, know, and use graphic visualization techniques to improve spatial vision linked to engineering.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: The Graphic Language of Technique
Topic 5: Incidence Relationships in Dihedral System
Topic 7: Fundamentals of the Cotated System
Topic 8: Incidence Relationships in Cotated System
Topic 11: Standardization and Norms in Engineering
Topic 20: Drawing of installations and processes
assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade is 0.5 * ETP1 + 0.1 * PA + 0.2 * PL + 0.2 * TIG, provided minimums are met. A minimum of 5 out of 10 is required for the final exam (ETP1) and for the average grade of laboratory practices (PL). If minimums are not met, the final grade is the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary calls, the final grade is 0.5 * ETP2 + 0.1 * PA + 0.2 * EPL + 0.2 * TIG, with a minimum of 5 out of 10 required for the final exam (ETP2) and the laboratory practices exam (EPL).
